citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang, Fien De Meulder (CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp)
description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, covering English and German. It includes training, development, and test splits annotated with four named entity types (persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous), along with large unannotated data files. English data is sourced from Reuters news stories and German data from the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper.
name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
publisher: CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation at the University of Antwerp
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not already in the other categories (persons, locations, organizations). Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another, usually only the top level entity is annotated. The IOB tagging scheme (Ramshaw and Marcus, 1995) was used.
rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. The German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau. Named entity tagging of training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: English raw data: Reuters news stories (Reuters Corpus). German raw data: texts from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau, extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. The unannotated data contain 17 million tokens (English) and 14 million tokens (German).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: training and development set from end of August 1996; test set from December 1996; unannotated data from September 1996. German: training, development and test sets from one week at the end of August 1992; unannotated data from September to December 1992.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
rai:dataUseCases: Named entity recognition (NER) system development and evaluation, particularly for language-independent NER. The dataset was used for training and evaluating machine learning systems that identify persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous named entities in text.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT tagger (memory-based tagger by Daelemans et al., 2002) for English POS tagging and chunking; Treetagger (decision tree tagger by Schmid, 1995) for German lemmatization, POS tagging and chunking.
